title: Dinner Rolls
description: Classic dinner rolls from an egg-enriched dough with a full stick of butter in it, plus more brushed on after baking.
source: Started from Chef John's Parker House Rolls, heavily modified since — https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/8514987/chef-johns-parker-house-rolls/

notes: Reference split: 24 rolls, matching the recipe yield.

Assumes 120 g flour per cup (540 g total), whole milk at 122 g per ½ cup, a 7 g yeast packet, 50 g per large egg, 12.5 g sugar per tbsp, and 14.2 g butter per tbsp. Extra flour added while kneading is not counted.
Counts all 12 tbsp butter as eaten: 8 in the dough, 4 brushed on after baking. The film of butter greasing the bowl and pan is not counted.
Water, salt and MSG add no macros.

ingredients.label: Whole milk
ingredients.sourceLabel: USDA SR28, NDB 01077: MILK,WHL,3.25% MILKFAT,W/ ADDED VITAMIN D

ingredients.label: Active dry yeast
ingredients.sourceLabel: USDA SR28, NDB 18375: LEAVENING AGENTS,YEAST,BAKER'S,ACTIVE DRY

directions.title: Bloom the yeast
directions.text: Warm the milk and water together in a measuring cup. About 45 seconds in a standard microwave gets you to the ~110°F you want. Into the stand mixer bowl with the yeast and let it sit 10 minutes. Melt the 8 tbsp dough butter while you wait.

directions.title: Mix and knead
directions.text: Once the yeast is bloomed, all the wets go in the bowl: the eggs, sugar, 8 g salt, 0.5 g MSG and the 8 tbsp melted butter. Make sure the butter has cooled enough that it won't cook the eggs when you pour it in. Whisk it together briefly with a fork. Dump in the flour and knead with the dough hook until it comes together into a ball, about 6 minutes. Add a little more flour only if it's not coming together.

directions.title: Bulk rise
directions.text: Into a lightly buttered bowl, covered, until doubled, 1 to 1.5 hours. The bulk rise isn't the most important part, so don't sweat it.

directions.title: Divide and shape
directions.text: Clean countertop, no flour, water or oil needed. Press the dough flat and cut it into a 6x4 grid, 24 pieces. No need to weigh anything. Squish each piece into a flat square and fold the 4 corners over onto each other so you've got a diamond, then fold those corners in again. Roll it briefly between your hands and now you have a ball.

directions.title: Proof
directions.text: Rub the baking vessel with a light amount of butter or some other fat. An aluminum or standard ceramic baking pan works perfectly; a sheet tray is fine too, and parchment isn't needed. Arrange the balls 6 by 4, cover with a clean towel and let rise somewhere warm until almost doubled, about 1 hour. This step is crucial: underproofed, they come out too dense and they're not good. Preheat the oven to 375°F toward the end.

directions.title: Bake
directions.text: Bake at 375°F until golden brown on top, about 25 minutes.

directions.title: Butter
directions.text: Brush the remaining 4 tbsp melted butter over the tops while they're still warm. It will look excessive, but it soaks in very quickly and it's important for the flavor. Sprinkle a little salt over the top if you want.

notes: This is derived from a Parker House roll recipe, so shape these however you wish. I don't bother with the fold. It's just as easy to rip a roll in half whether or not it's designed to do so.
No MSG? Leave it out, they're fine without. But may as well.
Browning the dough butter (with milk powder) doesn't do anything noticeable. Tried it, skip it.

deviations.why: The source amount is light. I like the salt level at 8 g.

deviations.what: 0.5 g MSG in with the salt
Shaped as plain round rolls instead of the Parker House fold, so the butter is all brushed on after baking instead of split with brushing before folding
deviations.why: Works fine as dinner rolls. It's just as easy to rip a roll in half.

deviations.what: Bake at 375°F instead of 350°F, same 25 minutes

log.entry: First bake, for the trial Thanksgiving. Bulk rise was doubled at about 1.5 hours, so moved on early.

Second bake. Browned the dough butter with 40 g milk powder, quenched with about 2 tbsp water. Worked fine, flavor isn't super pronounced in the finished rolls, as expected. 8 g salt + 2 g MSG: like the salt level, MSG is too much, dialing back to 0.5 g. Baked at 375°F for 25 minutes, perfect doneness.
Made it again. I think the recipe is perfect and dialed in now.
